Then from the base colour texture plug the "A" parameter of the RGBA in the opacity mask. The listing at Historic England (https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1064181) says: "In the west wall is reset a mid C12 tympanum with central scene of recumbent figures with triciput above. On the lintel beneath are chip carved star motifs. In the arch over are roundels containing geometric designs."

The Corpus of ROMANESQUE SCULPTURE in Britain & Ireland (https://www.crsbi.ac.uk/view-item?i=4864) says: 'Mee, writing in 1949, notes that the “unusual carving” of this tympanum consists of a “weird group of what appear to be men’s heads, a dragon, and a man fallen down, with the head of a lamb in the midst.” Binnall, on the other hand, interprets the central sculptural group as three connected heads “that may form an emblem of the Trinity” and a “recumbent figure…related to the Creation.” Zarnecki, whose opinion Binnall sought, did not commit to Binnall’s interpretation but suggested that if the heads symbolized the Trinity then the recumbent figure more likely represented “the force of evil overcome by the Trinity" (see Binnall). Pevsner laconically notes “a recumbent figure and the signum triciput” and is clearly following Binnall’s Trinitarian interpretation. The severe, weathered condition of the sculpture makes it extremely difficult to come to any conclusive interpretation of the iconography.'

I'm not sure, even after some googling, what "triciput" or "signum triciput" is about. There is a discussion of a Titian painting (https://www.jstor.org/stable/863048) where it is said to refer to a three-headed motif symbolising past, present and future, as embodied by Prudence.

i love your models man, how do you do the texturing? i want to have a very similar style to your models.

@random_guy1034 Thanks. For this scene I wasn't really creating textures, I was using google map 3D data. I modelled low poly buildings using the scanned geometry and then baked the textures into the low poly geometry. The challenging part was trying to figure out how to reduce all the bad distortions in the textures and make it look visually appealing. So I tried many techniques in Substance Designer, such as shadow removing, colour balancing and colour masking so that I can create windows that light up. I then just went back to blender and started placing spotlights to make the streets light up, and again, baked everything into a texture. It does take quite some experience with this, but this is pretty much a brief overview.
@99.Miles Ah, interesting, what about some of your other models? do you always use similar ways of doing stuff like this.
@random_guy1034 some of my older stuff was using simple photo texturing. My newer stuff involves me creating the textures using photoshop or substance
